Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Finance asked us to send our standard PO template (attached) and a couple of clarifying questions so they can start setup in our ERP:

- Can Redwood accept a single master PO with line-item sub-ledgers (our ERP will push separate invoice lines but reference one PO number)?
- We usually run Net45 but can consider Net60 if needed — are there pricing/discount implications for Net60 vs Net45?
- We also need an invoice cadence option (weekly vs monthly) so our AP team can map payment runs.

For context: this would be an initial 12-month commitment with a Q1 ramp estimate in Q4. Please advise what fields you need in the PO (e.g., PO number, BU code, project code, tax IDs).

Hi Lynn — appreciate the template. Attaching our PO guidelines for your ERP team; below are answers to your questions and a few asks so the onboarding doesn't stall: 

1) Single master PO with line-item sub-ledgers: yes, we can consume a single PO number and process separate invoice lines as long as each invoice references the PO and includes a line-item identifier we can map (we typically map on PO# + line description).

2) Net terms impact on pricing: our standard public pricing assumes Net30. For Net45 we can offer the baseline list pricing; Net60 typically triggers a small fee (we call it a financing uplift) — however, for committed annual spend (your expected Q1 ramp + 12-month commitment) we can hold Net60 at the same list price if you take the Tier 2 commitment band. I'll outline the bands below.

3) Invoice cadence: we support weekly, bi-weekly, and monthly invoice streams. Weekly creates more ledger chatter; for most clients we recommend monthly with a weekly interim statement if your AP needs frequent visibility.

Required PO fields (minimum): PO number, bill-to legal name, remit address, tax ID, invoice contact email, and a line-item identifier or SKU. Optional but helpful: internal BU code, cost center/project code.

Discount bands (example):
- Tier 1: annual commit <$250k — standard list pricing
- Tier 2: annual commit $250k–$750k — 8% discount (or same list at Net60)
- Tier 3: annual commit >$750k — 12% discount + priority capacity pool

I'll loop Vanessa for the billing mechanics and Marissa for PO acceptance flow and ledger mapping. If you can surface an estimated monthly invoice volume and whether your ERP requires a separate PO per legal entity, that will help.

Best,
Sean Gallagher\Head of Revenue Operations\Redwood Inference

Hi Lynn — quick follow-up on the mapping side.

We can accept the single master PO approach. For clean automation please: 
- Put the PO number in the invoice header and include a column called "WB Line ID" for your sub-ledger lines.
- If your ERP emits separate invoices per legal entity, include the remit address and tax ID on each invoice.

Regarding billing: we can do monthly invoicing with weekly CSV statements (no charge) so AP has visibility without creating invoices every week. For Net60 with no pricing uplift we need the Tier 2 commitment band confirmed in writing (simple clause in the contract amendment or an email from procurement confirming expected annual spend).

Attachment: Q4-Commitment-Estimate.xlsx — if you can fill the projected usage by month, we can confirm the applicable tier and produce a discount amendment to include with the PO.

Next steps: Lynn — can you confirm whether WellBridge will require one PO per legal entity or a single cross-entity PO? If single, please confirm that the single PO will carry the master remit information and each invoice will include the entity-specific tax IDs.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz\Senior Finance Ops Manager\Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q4-Commitment-Estimate.xlsx
